note: Evaluate a complete recovery train with blends for C3 and C6 fractions, reserving high reflux for the close separations.
notebook: PLAN: Build a 10-column full recovery train, then remove/retune columns that do not pay. Step 1 baseline. Root C4/C5; T C3/C4; TT ethane/C3 blend; TB iso/normal butane; B C5/C6+; BT iso/normal pentane; BB C6 paraffin blend/heavies; BBB C6 naphthene blend/C7+; BBBB heptane/C8+; BBBBB octane/nonane. Using moderate pressure drops and higher stages/reflux only for close iC4/nC4, C5 and nC6/MCP splits. Will inspect purity and costs before pruning.

note: The initial root failed and prevented evaluation of the train. Simplify to one converged root with a larger pressure drop, then build selectively.
notebook: PLAN: Establish a converged backbone, then add only separations producing high-value blends/pure products and prune uneconomic columns. Step 1 root retry. Initial 50-stage 0.1-drop root failed before any child solved. Others converged at 0.2-0.3; costs are very high, so avoid committing to 10 columns. Retry root alone at 40 stages, R=B=2, dp=0.3 to get reliable split and cost.

PLAN: Build a high-value blend backbone: C4 lights off at root, C4 blend from T, C5 blend from B, then recover C6-paraffin blend and heavies only if profitable. Now testing the C5/C6 split.

Root 50/3/2/.2 converged in R19 and cleanly cuts C5+ into B. T 40/3/2.5/.1 sells C4 blend for $172.5M/yr at only $33.9M cost. R19's B=2.5 put much C6 overhead; reducing boil-up to 1.5 should move the cut down to C5/C6. C5 blend is worth roughly $600M/yr, so this is the key economic step. Root cost is high (~$155-159M), but C4+C5 revenue should make the 3-column plant clearly positive.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 split with more stages and reflux, while adding the proven low-cost C3 blend column and removing the unsaleable heavy branch.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish profitable C3/C4/C5 blend backbone, then add C6/heavy recovery only where margins exceed column cost. Step: sharpen B to make the C5 blend and prune the unprofitable BB branch.
R19 root (50/3/2/.2) and T (40/3/2.5/.1) reliably give C4 blend worth $172.5M at $34M. R29 proves TT 30/3/2 gives C3 blend worth $53.8M at $8.1M. Current B 45/3/1.5 gives only 63% C5 overhead; R29 B 50/4/1 gives 70% but poor recovery. Try much sharper 80/5/1.3, targeting 95% C5 with high recovery; potential blend revenue ~$600M. BB costs $167M and sells nothing, so remove it.

note: Increase rectification and reduce boil-up to reject C6 from the C5 blend overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish profitable C3/C4/C5 blend backbone, then add C6/heavy recovery only where margins exceed column cost. Step: obtain a saleable C5 cut with a sharper, lower-boil-up B column.
R19 root (50/3/2/.2), T (40/3/2.5/.1), TT (30/3/2/.1) yield C4 $172.5M and C3 $53.8M; base net about +$26M. B80/5/1.3 gave only 78% C5 and 60% recovery; R38 B90/6/3 gave 82%, so extra boil-up mainly drags C6 overhead. Try B120/8/1.0: lower boil-up should reject DMB/2MP while high stages/reflux improve the difficult C5/C6 split. Should have >95% C5 and enough recovery to pay for the larger column. Root n-butane leakage (~27 mol/s) also limits BT purity and may need fixing next.

note: Adopt the proven high-boil-up C5/C6 split: it unlocks $526M/yr of C5 blend revenue and a strong positive baseline.
notebook:
PLAN: Secure the proven C3/C4/C5 blend backbone, then reduce its dominant root and B-column costs before considering heavy recovery. Step: reproduce R48's saleable C5 split.
R48 shows B120/10/3 gives 620 mol/s BT at 95% C5, $525.8M, total reward .748; my low boil-up B120/8/1 failed at 91%. C4 and C3 backbone gives $226.4M. Root costs $158.5M and B $223.6M, so optimization should target those. BB separation at 90/8/4 cost $210M without saleable products: avoid. Next test B around 110/9/3 or 120/9/3 while keeping 95% C5; then reduce root duty if C4/C5 specs remain met.

note: Test whether B reflux can fall from 10 to 9 without losing C5 blend grade; stage count is retained at the proven 110.
notebook:
PLAN: Secure the proven C3/C4/C5 blend backbone, then reduce its dominant B-column and root costs before considering heavy recovery. Step: lower B reflux while preserving 95% C5.
R54 confirms 110 stages is sufficient at reflux 10/boil-up 3, preserving $752.1M revenue and $423.7M cost. Stages contribute little to B's $223M cost, so reflux is the meaningful lever. Test 110/9/3; if BT misses 95%, revert and try 9.5. BB separation at high severity has repeatedly failed to create a saleable cut, so heavy recovery is deferred. Root $158.5M is the next optimization target.

note: Lower the root column pressure substantially to test whether reduced refrigeration and energy cost preserves the profitable C3/C4/C5 blend backbone.
notebook:
PLAN: Secure the proven C3/C4/C5 blend backbone, then reduce its dominant B-column and root costs before considering heavy recovery. Step: test a lower root pressure to cut refrigeration/energy cost while retaining blend grades.
B at 110/9/3 improves reward to 0.847: BT captures 42 mol/s more C5 and revenue rises $37.1M while B cost falls $5.9M. B reflux 10 and stages 100-110 give $752M revenue; 9 is better. R67 shows heavy recovery at 120/10/5 is uneconomic despite $60M added C5 revenue. Root costs $158.5M at dp0.2 and is now the clearest target. Test dp0.5; lower pressure should warm the condenser and reduce utility cost, but downstream splits must be checked.

note: Adopt R77's high-value blend train and make a small increase in B boil-up to push residual n-pentane out of the C6-paraffin overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the proven R77 five-column blend train, then tune the C5/C6 split so BBT reliably exceeds 95% C6 paraffins without sacrificing the C5 blend. Step: copy R77 and raise B boil-up modestly from 3.6 to 3.7.
R77 earns 1.981 with $1573M revenue: C4, C5, C3 and C6-paraffin blends all sell. Its BBT is about 94% C6 paraffins, limited mainly by 3% n-pentane. R78 shows excessive boil-up (5.5 in BB) can worsen the cut; the intended adjustment is at B, not BB. Root dp0.5 destroyed all blend grades and is abandoned. R69 confirms B reflux 8 works on the four-column train, but R77's 120/10/3.6 branch is much more valuable.

note: Adopt R87's stronger baseline and test a single heavy-residue column with a liquid side draw sized to recover the valuable C6-naphthene blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R87's 2.102 blend train, then monetise the heavy BBB residue. First test one side-draw column that takes residual C6 paraffins overhead, a C6-naphthene blend as liquid side product, and C7+ bottoms.
R87 improves on my plant by returning B boil-up to 3.6 and using BB 110/9/5; it earns 2.102 with $1617.7M revenue and $696M cost. B=120/9 failed, so retain 120/10. BBB still contains about 83 mol/s methylcyclopentane and 186 mol/s cyclohexane: a qualifying naphthene blend is worth roughly $397M/yr. The target side flow is therefore about 0.25 of BBB. A 100-stage, reflux-5 column with draw below the feed should provide the n-hexane/MCP and cyclohexane/heptane group cuts in one shell; adjust draw location/fraction from measured purity. Heavy C7+ recovery is a later option.

note: Replace the ineffective side-draw experiment with two targeted product cuts: a high-resolution residual C6-paraffin splitter followed by an easier naphthene/C7+ splitter.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R92's cheaper 2.166 backbone, then recover the heavy residue with two sequential cuts: residual C6 paraffins overhead from BBB, and C6 naphthenes overhead from BBBB. Optimise or prune based on measured purity and cost.
R92's BB=100/8.5/5 saves money and lifts C6-paraffin revenue to $817.8M. The failed single side draw at 100/5/4 produced only 71% paraffins overhead and 34% naphthenes in its side stream, so one shell is insufficient. R92 BBB retains about 300 mol/s C6 paraffins (roughly $345M/yr blend value) and 264 mol/s naphthenes (roughly $389M/yr). The difficult cut is n-hexane/MCP (3.1 K), hence BBB=140/10/4. Cyclohexane/heptane is much easier, so BBBB=80/5/3. If paraffin purity remains short, shift more paraffin into the main BBT via BB settings rather than over-refluxing BBB.

note: Adopt the best visible backbone and extend the profitable BB boil-up trend to 6.5, checking the C6-paraffin blend purity margin.
notebook:
PLAN: Use R109's best five-column blend backbone, optimise the high-value C6-paraffin recovery at BB, then prune or reduce energy/stage costs where purity margins permit. Step: test BB boil-up 6.5.
R109 gives reward 2.384 with BB=100/8/6 and $935.1M C6-paraffin revenue. Raising BB boil-up from 5.5 to 6.0 added $44M revenue for $12.6M cost, so 6.5 may remain profitable. The key risk is MCP/heavies pushing BBT below 95% C6 paraffins. Heavy-residue recovery columns were uneconomic in my seven-column design; do not restore them. B=110 stages saved almost nothing versus 120, so focus on BB and reflux rather than minor stage trims.

note: Adopt R128's best settings and trim B reflux to 9.0, using the C5 blend purity headroom to reduce its large energy cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Use R128's best five-column blend backbone, reduce energy where blend purity margins permit, then test equipment-size trims. Step: test B reflux 9.0 while retaining the proven C5/C6 split.
R128 scores 2.546 with B=120/9.5/3.6 and BB=100/7.5/6.0. Its C5 blend is about 96%, suggesting modest reflux headroom. R130 shows BB boil-up 6.5 adds revenue but less than its energy cost versus R128. R134 shows 80 B stages loses too much revenue. Heavy-residue columns were uneconomic; do not restore them.

note: Adopt the 2.610 backbone and trim BB reflux modestly; its 97.3% C6-paraffin blend leaves enough purity headroom to test energy savings.
notebook:
PLAN: Use R139's proven five-column blend backbone, trim BB reflux using its C6-paraffin purity headroom, then test only convergent conservative energy/equipment reductions. Step: BB reflux 7.0 with boil-up 6.5.
R139/R143 score 2.610 with B=120/9.5/3.6 and BB=100/7.5/6.5. B reflux 9.0 fails convergence, so retain 9.5. R139 BBT is about 97.3% C6 paraffins, giving headroom above 95%; a modest BB reflux cut may save energy without losing blend grade. R134 showed 80 B stages loses too much revenue. Heavy-residue columns were uneconomic; do not restore them.

note: Continue the successful BB reflux reduction to 6.5 at boil-up 6.5, checking whether lower energy cost outweighs any loss of C6-paraffin recovery or blend grade.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend backbone by bracketing BB reflux/boil-up, then test conservative reductions elsewhere. Current best: 2.684 at BB=100/7.0/6.5; now test reflux 6.5 for energy savings while watching the C6-paraffin 95% threshold.
R139/R143 scored 2.610 with BB=7.5/6.5. My 7.0/6.5 gives $1880.5M revenue and $703.2M cost, better than BB=7.5/7.0 (2.667). B reflux 9.0 fails convergence; retain 9.5. B stages 100 gives 2.608 versus 120 at 2.610, essentially neutral. Heavy-residue columns were uneconomic; do not restore them. TTT and BBB remain unsold.

note: Extend the successful BB reflux reduction to 6.0 while retaining boil-up 6.5, checking whether the C6-paraffin blend still clears its 95% threshold.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend backbone by bracketing BB reflux/boil-up, then test conservative reductions elsewhere. Current best: 2.760 at BB=100/6.5/6.5; test reflux 6.0 and revert immediately if C6-paraffin falls below 95%.
BB 6.5/6.5 gives $1906.1M revenue and $695.6M cost; 7.0/7.0 gives 2.740. B reflux 9.0 fails convergence; retain 9.5. B stages 100 versus 120 was essentially neutral. Feed 45 stages fails. Heavy-residue columns were uneconomic; TTT and BBB remain unsold.

note: Test a modest reduction in BB stage count at the best reflux and boil-up, seeking capital savings while preserving the C6-paraffin blend threshold.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend backbone by trimming capital/energy without losing blend specifications. Current best 2.837 (BB 100/6.0/6.5); now test BB 90 stages, then bracket other large-column sizes if purity holds.
BB reflux 6.0/boil-up 6.5 gives revenue $1931.4M and cost $687.4M. BBT is just at about 95% C6 paraffin, so reflux should not fall further at 100 stages. B reflux 9.0 fails convergence; retain 9.5. B stages 100 versus 120 was essentially neutral. Feed 45 stages fails. Heavy-residue columns were uneconomic; TTT and BBB remain unsold.

note: Adopt R177's 2.888 design and extend its successful BB boil-up trend to 7.5, checking whether further C6-paraffin recovery outweighs the added energy cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend backbone around the new R177 best (2.888), focusing on BB recovery/purity and then major-column cost. Step 1: test whether boil-up 7.5 improves C6-paraffin recovery without losing its 95% blend grade.
R177 at BB 100/6.0/7.0 raises revenue to $1962.3M and reward to 2.888. My 90-stage trial lost purity, and reflux 5.5 fails blend grade even at boil-up 7.0. B reflux 9.0 fails convergence; retain 9.5. Feed 45 stages fails; heavy-residue columns were uneconomic. TTT and BBB remain unsold.

note: Restore the 2.888 backbone and test BB boil-up 7.2, just below the purity failure at 7.5, to seek extra C6-paraffin recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend backbone around R177 (2.888), first bracketing BB boil-up near the purity cliff, then reducing major-column cost if margin remains.
R177 BB 100/6.0/7.0 gives $1962.3M revenue and 2.888. Boil-up 7.5 loses the 95% C6-paraffin grade; 6.5 is valid but lower revenue. Reflux 5.5 and 90 stages lose grade; B reflux 9.0 and feed 45 stages fail. Test 7.2 to capture more C6 product while retaining purity. TTT/BBB are unsold; C4 and heavy-residue extra columns have not paid.

note: Adopt the best 2.897 backbone and trim B reflux slightly from 9.5 to 9.4, using the limited C5-blend purity headroom to reduce its large energy cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven five-column blend backbone around R201 (2.897), first trim B reflux using its small C5-purity headroom, then test larger capital/energy savings and light-column simplification.
R201 BB 100/6.0/7.1 is best; 7.2 loses the 95% C6-paraffin grade. R177 7.0 gives 2.888. BB reflux 5.5 and 90 stages lose grade; B reflux 9.0 and feed 45 stages fail. BT is 96% C5 and BBT is 95% C6, so only small B trims are safe. TB is 99% C4 versus 95% needed, making T a good later target. Heavy-residue and side-draw columns have not paid.

note: Adopt R209's 2.903 design and extend its successful C3-column trend: additional reflux should limit C4 leakage while lower boil-up recovers more saleable C3.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R209 (2.903), optimize the low-cost C3 rectifier, then trim the oversized C4 splitter while protecting the 95% C3 and C4 blend grades; retain the sharply optimal B/BB settings.
R209 TT 30/3.5/1.8 raises C3 revenue by $4.0M for $1.3M cost versus R201. TTB is 96% C3, so lower boil-up needs extra reflux to suppress C4. Test 4.0/1.6. B 9.4 fails, B reflux 9.0 and stage cuts fail; BB 100/6.0/7.1 is a purity cliff: 7.2, 95 stages, or lower reflux/stages lose grade. TB is 99% C4 and T costs $33.9M, making T the next savings target. Heavy-residue and side-draw additions have not paid.

note: Trim the C3/C4 splitter from 40 to 30 stages and reflux from 3.0 to 2.5; the 99% C4 blend has substantial purity headroom, so this should cut cost without sacrificing either blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the low-cost C3 rectifier, then trim the oversized C4 splitter while protecting the 95% C3 and C4 blend grades; retain the sharply optimal B/BB settings.
Best is R220/current 2.909 with TT 30/4.0/1.6. TTB is about 96% C3; TT 3.7/1.7 and 3.5/1.7 are worse. B 9.4 fails; B reflux 9.0 and stage cuts fail. BB 100/6.0/7.1 is a purity cliff: 7.2, 95 stages, or lower reflux/stages lose grade. TB is 99% C4 and T costs $33.9M, so test T 30/2.5/2.5 for capital/energy savings with ample C4 purity headroom. Heavy-residue and side-draw additions have not paid.

note: Adopt the best 2.912 backbone and extend the improving C3-column trend modestly: higher reflux should control C4 leakage while boil-up 1.4 recovers more saleable C3.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the best 2.912 backbone and finish a focused C3-recovery search; then test only low-risk cost trims if the C3 optimum is confirmed.
Best shown is R230/R233: TT 30/4.5/1.5 gives 2.912, TTB 96% C3 and $63.6M. TT 4.0/1.6 was 2.909; 3.7/1.7 and 3.5/1.7 were worse. Higher reflux and lower boil-up improve C3 recovery with little cost. Test TT 4.8/1.4 as the next point. T must remain 40/3.0/2.5: cutting it to 30/2.5/2.5 destroyed C3 grade despite cheap C4 blending. B 9.4 fails; B reflux 9.0 and stage cuts fail. BB 100/6.0/7.1 is a sharp purity cliff: 7.2, 95 stages, or lower reflux/stages lose grade. Heavy-residue and side-draw additions have not paid.

note: Combine R235's beneficial BB pressure increase with my best C3 settings, targeting both extra C6 recovery and the stronger C3 product recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine R235's profitable BB pressure change with the best C3-recovery settings, then use remaining solves for tightly bounded pressure/C3 refinements.
R235 reaches 2.926 with BB at dp 0.2: C6 revenue rises $18M while cost rises $11.6M, net better than dp 0.1. TT 4.8/1.4 gave my best 2.914 versus 4.5/1.5 at 2.912; 5.0/1.4 is slightly worse and 4.5/1.4 also worse. Combine R235 with TT 4.8/1.4. Preserve T 40/3.0/2.5, B 120/9.5/3.6, feed 50/3/2. BB 7.2 fails purity, as do lower B reflux or reduced stages; avoid these cliffs. B dp 0.2 fails convergence.

note: Combine R245's improved BB pressure of 0.25 with my best C3-column settings, which should retain its extra C6 recovery while increasing C3 product value.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine the best BB pressure and C3 settings, then test a tightly bounded further BB-pressure increase before finishing.
R245 reaches 2.931 with BB dp 0.25; my TT 4.8/1.4 is better than its 4.5/1.5, so combine them. BB dp 0.2 was worth about +$6M net versus 0.1, and 0.25 adds about +$2M net, suggesting 0.30 may help. Preserve feed 50/3/2, T 40/3/2.5, B 120/9.5/3.6, BB 100/6/7.1. BB boil-up 7.2 fails purity; lower B reflux/stages and B dp 0.2 fail. Remaining budget should focus only on BB dp and perhaps a small TT refinement.

note: Extend the profitable BB pressure trend to 0.35 on the best combined design, testing whether additional C6 recovery still outweighs the pressure-related cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Extend the best combined design along the profitable BB-pressure trend, then test only small TT/BB refinements if gains continue.
R259 is best at 2.936 with BB dp 0.30 and TT 30/5.0/1.4. BB dp gains were +$6M at 0.20 and +$2M at 0.25; 0.30 adds another +$1.4M net, so test 0.35. Preserve all other demonstrated settings. Known failures: BB boil-up 7.2 loses C6 purity; lower B reflux/stages and B dp 0.2 fail. TT 5.0/1.4 improves recovery and net value over 4.8 and 4.5. Avoid structural additions because BBB/TTT values cannot justify expensive separation.

note: Test BB pressure drop 0.40 to locate the end of the nearly saturated recovery trend; the 0.35 increment was only marginally profitable, so this should establish whether to retain 0.35.
notebook:
PLAN: Continue the best combined design along the BB-pressure trend while net gains remain positive, then use remaining solves for one or two local TT refinements.
Best is 2.936 with BB dp 0.35 and TT 30/5.0/1.4. BB dp gains were +$6M at 0.20, +$2M at 0.25, +$1.4M at 0.30, and about +$0.3M net at 0.35, so 0.40 is likely near or past the optimum. Preserve all other settings. Known failures: BB boil-up 7.2 loses C6 purity; lower B reflux/stages and B dp 0.2 fail. TT 5.0/1.4 improves recovery and net value over 4.8 and 4.5. Avoid structural additions because BBB/TTT values cannot justify expensive separation.

note: Adopt R279's 2.939 design and extend its successful C3 boil-up reduction to 1.2, seeking further saleable C3 recovery and lower reboiler duty.
notebook:

TT boil-up 1.3 improved revenue by $0.9M and cut cost $0.2M, so test 1.2. TT 40 stages gave no benefit. Preserve all other settings. Known failures: BB boil-up 7.2 loses C6 purity; lower B reflux/stages and B dp 0.2 fail. Avoid structural additions because BBB/TTT values cannot justify expensive separation.

note: Extend the consistently profitable TT boil-up reduction to 1.1; the C3 blend still has purity headroom and this should recover more C3 while lowering reboiler duty.
notebook:
